note: Curated public-synthetic Operations Manual cases. Strict refusals require no grounded answer; safe-boundary cases require the cited pointer without invented procedure detail.

questions.question: When does Operations Manual Version 3.2 take effect, and which version does it supersede?
questions.rationale: Basic header retrieval; failure here indicates the chunker dropped the front-matter.

questions.question: How many warehouses, vehicles and employees does Northwind operate according to the manual?
questions.rationale: Three co-located numbers in one sentence; systems often return only one of the three figures.

questions.question: After how long does a printed copy of the Operations Manual become uncontrolled unless Quality stamps it as a Controlled Printed Copy?
questions.rationale: A short rule buried in document-control prose that is easy to miss if only the version header is retrieved.

questions.question: What is the maximum validity period of an interim control notice issued by the Head of Quality?
questions.rationale: Tests retrieval of a calendar-day (not Working Day) limit that sits in a short subsection.

questions.question: Within how many calendar days of the expense date must an expense claim normally be submitted?
questions.rationale: Straightforward figure that is easy to confuse with the 90-day Band 6+ late-claim threshold.

questions.question: What is the cash-advance limit per employee and by when must an advance be cleared after trip completion?
questions.rationale: Two related numbers in one paragraph; a weak retriever may return only the amount or only the clearance window.

questions.question: What is the maximum capital expenditure a Band 4–5 manager can approve?
questions.rationale: The value sits in Table 2.1 at the intersection of Capital expenditure and Band 4–5; poor table chunking often splits the header from the cell.

questions.question: What is the Band 6+ maximum for operating expenditure before Board approval is required?
questions.rationale: Must pick the Opex row, not Capex (€247,500) or Contract signing (€312,750), from a multi-row authority matrix.

questions.question: What IT procurement amount can a Band 4–5 manager approve under Version 3.2?
questions.rationale: The live table cell is €15,000; the amendment log still mentions the old €12,000 limit, so naive retrieval can return the superseded figure.

questions.question: For a budget variance between 5.0% and 7.9%, who is the approval authority and what is the reporting deadline?
questions.rationale: Table 2.2 has six adjacent percentage bands with different authorities and deadlines; off-by-one row errors are common.

questions.question: What is the required response time for a Major incident with financial impact?
questions.rationale: Table 3.1 intersects severity with impact type; a chunk that has only the Major row or only the Financial column will miss the cell.

questions.question: What safety-impact response time applies to a Critical incident?
questions.rationale: Must distinguish Critical safety (1 hour) from Critical financial (2 hours) in the same table row.

questions.question: How often must pharmaceuticals be cycle-counted and what accuracy is required?
questions.rationale: The cycle-count table has five stock categories with similar weekly/fortnightly frequencies; the 99.9% pharma cell is easy to swap with 99.7% high-value stock.

questions.question: What temperature range and maximum excursion time apply to Category A frozen biologics?
questions.rationale: Table 4.1 is long and wrapped; Category A numbers can be mixed with Category B (+2°C to +8°C / 30 minutes).

questions.question: How long must cold chain temperature records be retained?
questions.rationale: Table 7.1 lists many retention periods; the live value is 10 years but Appendix A still records the old 7-year period.

questions.question: What is the retention period for Critical Incident investigation files compared with ordinary incident files?
questions.rationale: A single table cell contains two periods (8 years; Critical Incidents 12 years); chunkers often keep only one.

questions.question: Can temporary staff operate forklifts?
questions.rationale: The default rule is no; the exception requires a valid RTITB certificate, module NWFLT-02 within 90 days, and a passed site practical assessment, which may live in a different sentence or chunk.

questions.question: Do contracts above €25,000 always need two signatories?
questions.rationale: The two-signatory rule and the Board-pre-approved Framework Agreement exception are in the same subsection but can be split across chunks.

questions.question: Must a buyer obtain three written quotes for an €9,000 spare part bought from the original equipment manufacturer of a safety-critical component?
questions.rationale: €9,000 is above the €7,500 three-quote threshold, but OEM safety-critical parts are an exception alongside Framework Agreements and Emergency Purchases.

questions.question: If an inbound seal is broken on an internal shuttle transfer that has electronic seal verification and no customer chain-of-custody requirement, must unloading stop?

any_of: no customer chain of custody requirement

questions.rationale: The default broken-seal rule is stop-and-notify; the internalshuttle exception is a trailing clause that is often chunked away from the rule.

questions.question: Can alcohol ever be claimed on expenses?
questions.rationale: The headline rule is 'Alcohol is not reimbursable' and the hospitality exception with the €85 cap is in the same sentence after an em-dash.

questions.question: If a driver finds a safety-critical defect, may they move the vehicle at all?
questions.rationale: Default is immobilise; the only exception is a move of less than 500 metres to leave live traffic or immediate danger.

questions.question: Does a Local Legal Addendum automatically override the manual if the addendum is 20 months old and has not been reviewed?
questions.rationale: The addendum applies except when it has expired, lacks Legal approval, or is older than 18 months without review — three negative conditions that must all be checked.

questions.question: If the Site Duty Manager is unreachable for 20 minutes during a Critical Incident, must the reporter wait, or contact the Regional Operations Control Desk?
questions.rationale: The 15-minute bypass rule itself has a further exception if calling the desk would delay medical response, evacuation, spill containment or firealarm activation.

questions.question: A 12.5% adverse budget variance is confirmed at month-end close. Who must be notified and by when?
questions.rationale: Table 2.2 (12.0%–17.4% band) must be combined with the COO-and-CFO / within-24-hours-of-confirmation rule in the same table, not the 17.5% Board-within-5-calendar-days row.

questions.question: A vehicle accident involves injury and projected loss of €30,000. Which incident framework must be used to classify it?
questions.rationale: Section 5.5.1 sends the reader to Section 3.1 / Appendix B; the system must follow that cross-reference rather than inventing a fleet-only severity.

questions.question: When newly received cold-chain equipment arrives, what must be checked before it is released for use, and which section governs that check?
questions.rationale: Goods-receipt (2.2.4) only points to calibration evidence in 4.3.5; both chunks must be retrieved to state that calibration certificates are required before release.

questions.question: If a customer contract conflicts with this manual, what rule applies until Legal issues a written instruction, and how quickly must the conflict be notified?
questions.rationale: Section 1.1 and Section 2.5.4 both discuss contract conflicts; the operational default is the stricter rule and notification is due within 2 Working Days.

questions.question: A Category B chilled-pharmaceutical excursion is detected. After quarantining stock, which incident-classification appendix should Quality use if released stock may have been affected?
questions.rationale: Section 4.3.2 points to Section 3.1 and Appendix B for classification; product-integrity rows in Appendix B must be joined with the 30-minute Category B limit in Table 4.1.

questions.question: Does an IT tool that costs €800 and will store customer route data still need Information Security review before purchase?
questions.rationale: Table 2.1 Band 1–3 IT limit is €1,200 so cost alone would pass, but 2.2.2 and 7.4.5 require Security review whenever Northwind data is stored, regardless of the Table 2.1 threshold.

questions.question: How does the fleet accident-and-breakdown escalation path relate to the general incident path?
questions.rationale: Section 3.4.3 states that the Section 3.4 path applies to 5.5 accidents as modified by 5.5.2; both sections must be retrieved together.

questions.question: A supervisor in Madrid discovers a data-protection observation at 21:00 on a Spanish public holiday that is not a Belgian public holiday. By when must it be logged?
questions.rationale: Observations are normally 72 hours, but security/dataprotection observations must be logged within 24 hours, and Working Day is defined on Belgian — not local — holidays.

questions.question: An employee reports an equipment malfunction at 16:00. The manual says the matter must be handled Immediately. What is the latest clock time that still complies?
questions.rationale: Immediately is a defined term meaning within 4 hours of discovery, including outside office hours, and not 4 hours after the next shift starts.

questions.question: A chilled room briefly reads +9°C for four minutes then returns to +6°C. Is that a Temperature Excursion?
questions.rationale: The defined threshold is more than 5 consecutive minutes outside range; four minutes is not an excursion even though +9°C is outside the +2°C to +8°C Category B band.

questions.question: A person titled 'Operations Manager' at Band 6 is on site during an incident. Are they automatically the Incident Commander?
questions.rationale: Senior Manager means any Band 6+ employee regardless of title, but Incident Commander is defined as the currently certified assignee, not the most senior person present.

questions.question: Expected financial exposure is €260,000 with no injuries. Does this meet the definition of a Critical Incident?
questions.rationale: Critical is defined in Section 1.2 as including financial exposure above €250,000; Appendix B uses the same threshold and the system must apply the definition rather than treat it as Major (€50,001–€250,000).

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted excursion time for Category B chilled pharmaceuticals under Version 3.2?
questions.rationale: Version 3.1 allowed 45 minutes; returning 45 minutes is a precise but obsolete number that the amendment log still contains.

questions.question: What overtime multipliers apply to scheduled Saturday warehouse work versus Sunday warehouse work?
questions.rationale: Common assumption is a flat 1.5× weekend rate (the Version 3.1 rule); the live rates are 1.20× for the first 6 Saturday hours, 1.45× thereafter, and 1.60× on Sunday.

questions.question: For how long may dock doors remain open during cold-chain loading if there is no air curtain or sealed dock shelter?
questions.rationale: Nearby numbers include 10-minute re-checks, 20-minute loading trigger, and 15/30/20-minute pre-cool times; only 7 minutes is the open-door cap.

questions.question: What are the minimum pre-cooling times for frozen, chilled and controlled-ambient vehicles before loading?
questions.rationale: Three different minute values (45 / 30 / 20) must be paired with the correct vehicle class; mixing them is a common numerical error.

questions.question: What is the minimum password length required by the information-security settings in this manual?
questions.rationale: Generic password knowledge (8 or 12 characters) will override the manual's explicit 14-character rule if the chunk is missed.

questions.question: What was the permitted Category B cold-chain excursion time before the Version 3.2 update?
questions.rationale: The current body states 30 minutes; the old 45-minute value lives only in Appendix A amendment AM-3.2-001 and is easy to overwrite with the live rule.

questions.question: Which Board decision authorised the increase in the Band 4–5 IT procurement limit?
questions.rationale: The authorising reference exists only in the amendment-log Reason column, not in Table 2.1 itself.

questions.question: Why was the term Immediately given a definition in Version 3.2, and what audit finding drove that change?
questions.rationale: Requires retrieving AM-3.2-003 from Appendix A rather than restating the current 4-hour definition from Section 1.2.

questions.question: How long were cold-chain temperature records retained under Version 3.1, and what CAPA reference justified extending that period?
questions.rationale: The live Table 7.1 says 10 years; the prior 7-year period and CAPA GDP-2026-044 appear only in AM-3.2-006.

questions.question: What new budget-variance tier did Version 3.2 add below the previous 5% escalation starting point?
questions.rationale: AM-3.2-008 / FIN-2026-027 must be read against Table 2.2; a system that only reads the current table will not know what was added.

questions.question: Which types of decision have a Band 1–3 maximum of €0 in the delegation matrix?
questions.rationale: RAG prefers positive permissions; the question asks what Band 1–3 may NOT approve (capital expenditure, contract signing, headcount, fleet acquisition, lease commitment).

questions.question: May Quality release chilled pharmaceuticals after a temperature excursion based only on the product looking normal?

any_of: must not be released based only on visual inspection
not released based only on visual inspection

questions.rationale: Section 4.3.2 forbids release on visual inspection alone even if the customer requests urgent shipment; the negation is easy to drop.

questions.question: Does working a weekend warehouse shift automatically create a day-off entitlement the following week?
questions.rationale: The manual calls out that this differs from common informal practice; a model using prior HR knowledge will answer yes.

questions.question: Which five things may an interim control notice not do?
questions.rationale: The prohibition list (increase spending authority, waive incident reporting, reduce PPE, shorten retention, authorise unqualified drivers) is a negative constraint that chunkers often omit.

questions.question: List in order the eight purchase-request steps a requester must complete before a supplier is instructed.

any_of: Confirm the business need and budget code
specification, quote comparison and risk assessment
Confirm goods receipt or service completion

questions.rationale: Section 2.2.2 is an ordered eight-step list; dropping, reordering or merging steps (especially the wait-for-PO-release step) is a typical RAG failure.

questions.question: When a Temperature Excursion is detected, what is the ordered sequence of actions starting with stopping pick/load/dispatch?
questions.rationale: Eight numbered steps in 4.3.2 include a 15-minute quarantine SLA; retrieving a summary without order or the quarantine deadline fails the procedure.

questions.question: What is the complete escalation sequence for a Critical or Major incident, from the reporter through Communications?

any_of: Reporter notifies Shift Lead or Site Duty Manager

questions.rationale: Section 3.4.1 has nine ordered steps; skipping the certified Incident Commander appointment or swapping COO/CEO order is a common merge error.

questions.question: Walk through the receiving team's required steps from confirming the booking reference through moving goods to storage.
questions.rationale: Ten numbered receiving steps end with a 2-hour put-away SLA; partial retrieval that omits seal check or quarantine status is insufficient.

questions.question: After a road accident, what ordered actions must the driver take before considering liability statements?

any_of: Record location, time, parties, vehicle registrations and witness details
Photograph damage, road position and signage

questions.rationale: Section 5.5.1 is an eight-step list that also points to Section 6.3 testing; order matters (life first, notify Fleet Control within 30 minutes if safe, do not admit liability).

questions.question: What is the mandatory sequence of points in a Critical or Major incident escalation call?
questions.rationale: Appendix C.1 is a 10-line script; a model that paraphrases 'tell them what happened' without the prescribed order fails the procedural test.

questions.question: What is the CEO's annual salary?
questions.rationale: Compensation is outside this internal operations manual; the system must refuse rather than infer from Band 6+ delegation limits.

questions.question: What is the step-by-step disciplinary procedure for gross misconduct?
questions.rationale: Section 6.4 says the full procedure is a separate Controlled Document and that this manual does not replace it; answering with invented steps is a failure.

questions.question: What customer rate card applies to the pharmaceutical lane Antwerp–Lyon?
questions.rationale: Rate cards are cited as Restricted Information examples but no actual rates or lane prices appear in the manual.

questions.question: Does Operations Manual Section 6.5 specify exactly how many days an investigator has to interview the accused after an anonymous report, or does it defer the full procedure to a separate controlled document?
questions.rationale: Section 6.5 only points to GOV-POL-006; interview timelines are not in this manual and must not be invented.

questions.question: Which external ISO certification body audits Northwind's ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 systems?
questions.rationale: The manual requires alignment to ISO 9001/14001 but never names an auditor, certificate number or last audit date.

questions.question: Is it true that weekend warehouse overtime is paid at the standard 1.5× rate?
questions.rationale: Trick question: Version 3.1 used a standard 1.5× weekend rate (AM-3.2-005); the live rules split Saturday 1.20×/1.45× and Sunday 1.60×.

questions.question: The site's most senior Band 6 manager is present and certified Incident Commanders are not. Who leads the incident?
questions.rationale: Trick against hierarchy: if no certified Incident Commander is on site, the Control Desk assigns one remotely within 30 minutes (Critical) or 60 minutes (Major); seniority does not fill the gap.

questions.question: An employee in Spain wants to delay a Minor incident report until after a Spanish public holiday. Does Working Day allow that delay?

any_of: not the employee’s local public holidays
not the employee's local public holidays

questions.rationale: Trick question using the manual's own example: Working Day excludes Belgian public holidays, not the employee's local holidays.

questions.question: A driver fails a post-accident substance test. Which Operations Manual sections and which separate HR document jointly govern suspension from driving and the conduct process?
questions.rationale: Sections 5.5.1, 6.3 and 6.4 must be joined with HRPOL-014; the manual authorises immediate suspension from safety-sensitive duties but refuses to state the disciplinary steps.
